opening.argument: The presentation examines whether ultrasound can influence meditation and mindfulness through a proposed neurological mechanism, not through a financial or credential-collection offer. It explains that the procedure is intended to quiet a brain network and potentially accelerate meditation’s effects, while showing head-mounted equipment being adjusted and identifying the posterior cingulate cortex in an illustrated brain diagram. Crucially, the discussion expressly limits consumer use: “We might not be right at this point to just create... ...something that you sell on Amazon and tell people to use it every day. We just don't know if that's safe.” That stated uncertainty about safety is inconsistent with a risky product pitch. The closing requests to subscribe and support the publisher are ordinary engagement prompts, not evidence of a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: What we're targeting with ultrasound is quieting a brain network that is active in all of us.
We might not be right at this point to just create... ...something that you sell on Amazon and tell people to use it every day. We just don't know if that's safe.
